Theorem
[Higher global regularity] 1. ch6:6.19\group gt-ch06 If $\Omega $ is $C^{k+2,\alpha }$, $u\in C^0(\bar\Omega )\cap C^2(\Omega )$ solves $Lu=f$, $u=\varphi $ on $\partial \Omega $, and the coefficients, $f$, and $\varphi $ are in $C^{k,\alpha }(\bar\Omega )$, $C^{k,\alpha }(\bar\Omega )$, and $C^{k+2,\alpha }(\bar\Omega )$, then $u\in C^{k+2,\alpha }(\bar\Omega )$.
Proof

\sketch Lemma 6.18 is the base case. Flatten the boundary, take tangential difference quotients, and recover the normal second derivative from $D_{nn}u=(f-(L-a^{nn}D_{nn})u)/a^{nn}$. Induction gives the general case.

□
